approachQuestion.prompt:
Panel switches

A binary string describes n panels, where 0 is off and 1 is on. One operation chooses an index and toggles that panel and every panel to its right. Return the minimum operations needed to turn every panel off. There is no operation that toggles only an interior range.

Example 1: s="00110" → 2: toggle suffix at index 2, then suffix at index 4 (zero-based).
Example 2: s="111" → 1.
Example 3: s="000" → 0.

Constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; s contains only 0 and 1. Input is read-only. Return only the stated scalar result. All arithmetic and comparisons use constant-time exact 64-bit operations; all intermediate values fit.

options.text: Scan from left to right with flipParity initially zero. The current effective bit is the original bit toggled by flipParity. If it is 1, count an operation starting here and toggle flipParity. Otherwise move on.
options.feedback: After passing a position, no operation starting later can change it. If its effective value is 1 an operation at this position is forced; if it is 0 such an operation would undo a correct prefix. Only the parity of earlier operations matters.

options.text: Return the number of 1 characters in the original string.
options.feedback: One suffix operation can fix several adjacent ones. For "111" the answer is 1, not 3.

options.text: Return the number of maximal runs of 1 in the original string.
options.feedback: A run followed by zeros also requires restoring the trailing zero region. For "10" the answer is 2, not 1.

options.text: Make a mutable copy of the bits. Scan left to right; whenever a bit is 1, explicitly toggle every bit of the suffix beginning there.
options.feedback: The same forced choices are correct, but physically rewriting overlapping suffixes repeatedly adds avoidable work and a copied array. One parity bit represents those toggles.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed frontier method, regardless of your previous choice. Use exactly the frontier method above as iterative scans with scalar indices, counters and accumulators. Do not copy the input and do not store a decision list. Let n be the number of input records or positions. Choose the tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Input and returned scalar are excluded. All other live storage, including copying and any call stack, is counted. No hashing or expected-time operations are used.

feedback.reason: One effective-bit decision per position replaces repeated suffix mutations.

messages.text: The method stores no per-item history or copied input.
The scans do not restart for each item.
In the worst case every input item can affect the answer.

details: The scan reads each switch once and updates parity/count in constant work. It never loops across the affected suffix, so total time is O(n), not quadratic. Parity, count, and index require O(1) auxiliary space.
“Time O(n), auxiliary space O(n)”: The method stores no per-item history or copied input.
“Time O(n²), auxiliary space O(1)”: The scans do not restart for each item.
“Time O(1), auxiliary space O(1)”: In the worst case every input item can affect the answer.
